task: You support the operations director of a regional clinic network. Missed appointments waste clinician time, and finance is worried about unpaid costs and repeat emergency visits. Before the director funds a reminder service or a care-coordination pilot, find out how many bookings are missed, where no-shows are highest, who pays for care and how often emergency patients come back within 30 days.

produce.name: Appointment outcomes
produce.about: Appointments and share for each booking status.

produce.name: No-shows by specialty
produce.about: Past appointments, no-shows and no-show rate for each larger specialty.

produce.name: Payer mix
produce.about: Encounters, average cost and the share payers covered for each insurance type.

produce.name: Emergency returns
produce.about: Emergency patients, visits and returns within 30 days.

produce.name: Operations brief
produce.about: Three findings and one funding recommendation.

summaries.understand-data: Follow a completed appointment to its encounter, and find visits with no appointment.
summaries.appointment-outcomes: Count bookings that were completed, cancelled, missed or are still scheduled.
summaries.no-shows: Compare no-show rates across specialties with enough past appointments.
summaries.payer-mix: Measure how much billed cost payers cover for each insurance type.
summaries.emergency-returns: Find emergency visits followed by another within 30 days.
summaries.synthesis: Weigh the evidence for a reminder service against care coordination.
summaries.report: Write three findings and one funding recommendation.

problems: 22 appointments are still scheduled after the data ends, so they have no outcome yet.
Every emergency, inpatient and urgent-care visit has no appointment, so appointment counts miss them.
Cancelled and missed appointments link to no encounter.
Self-pay visits show nothing paid by a payer, so their whole cost is unpaid.
Three of the nine specialties have fewer than 200 past appointments, too few for a stable rate.
